analysis.file_name: GS Blekos - ## Marketcolour + Cross-Asset Outlook Copper ASML Fieldtrip Airtel (I) GTT & Technip ## 19 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: Marketcolour + Cross-Asset Outlook / Copper / ASML Fieldtrip / Airtel (I) / GTT & Technip
key_insights: US equities closed mixed on 11/18: SPX -23bps to 7323 (7 of 11 sectors up, Energy -325bps, Consumer Discretionary +184bps), NDX +42bps to 27116, RTY +46bps to 27236. Hyperscalers were firm (AMZN +3%, GOOG +1%).
In Europe, AI capex names held up (ASML +2%, STM +2%, IFX +1%) while most other sectors fell. Materials and energy led the declines as commodity prices fell globally.

GS cross-asset outlook is overweight SPX, TOPIX, 10Y UST and Gilts, and underweight USD high yield. It stays modestly pro-risk but favours more balance as nominal and earnings growth approach a peak after the 2026 AI capex boom and energy-driven inflation boost.

Near-term risks named in the GS outlook: AI concerns, renewed energy shocks, more aggressive Fed tightening and persistent fiscal concerns. GS expects the balance between slowing growth and rates relief to drive risk appetite in 2027.

Copper fell 5% on 11/18 on global growth concerns (BCOM -2%), bearish Chinese demand feedback from the Shanghai CESCO conference, and expectations of US exports, which triggered heavy short-selling on SHFE.

Bull case for copper: direct AI copper demand holds because capex is committed, scrap stays tight for at least two quarters, mine supply does not rebound in 2027, State Grid tenders are increasing into year end, and the US administration is expected to act on trade policy.
GS expects the Fed to hike 25bp in both December 2026 and March 2027 to a peak range of 4.25-4.5%, then cut gradually from November 2027 to a terminal range of 3.25-3.5%.
GS expects the ECB to hike 25bp in December to a peak policy rate of 2.75%, then normalize toward a 2.25% terminal rate in 4Q27.

ASML field trip takeaways: strong High NA momentum and ecosystem, a deep competitive moat, multiple avenues for output optimisation, strong installed base management and upgrades business, and Match Act concerns seen as overdone.
Airtel Africa initiation with a 260p price target (15% upside, 15x EBITDA). GS expects Airtel Money revenue ex-FX CAGR of about 26% over FY26-31E, driven by penetration and ARPU growth.

LNG: GS identifies about 280 mtpa of capacity reaching FID across 2025-30, up about 52 mtpa or 23% from about 228 mtpa in TP2026. GTT is the preferred LNG exposure (Buy, EUR 210 12-month PT, 12.4% upside). Technip Energies is removed from the Buy list and moved to Neutral, primarily on valuation after strong share-price performance.

UniCredit and the German government reached broad agreement on Commerzbank. Finance Minister Klingbeil said UniCredit made commitments on Germany as a business location, Commerzbank employees' rights and dialogue with the works council.

NKT Q3 operating EBITDA was 4% below consensus, with weaker top line in Transmission and Distribution on tough comps and timing effects. Guidance was maintained, with NKT expecting the high end of the range, about EUR 430m versus consensus EUR 424m, roughly a 1% upgrade.

Halma 1H organic growth was +12.3% versus consensus +11.5%, a roughly 5% beat, driven by Safety. E&A, which contains photonics, missed. Photonics grew 30% in 1H and is still guided to about 30% for the full year, which the note calls light given falling expectations.
GTA 6 launches 11/19 with over $1.65 billion in preorder sales, about 75% on PlayStation 5. Comcast and Virgin Media O2 reported record network traffic from preloads.

market_movers.rationale: Airtel Africa initiation with 15% upside at 15x EBITDA. Airtel Money expected to grow revenue ex-FX at about 26% CAGR over FY26-31E.
GTT is GS's preferred LNG exposure, with a 12.4% upside to the 12-month PT as LNG FID capacity rises about 23% versus TP2026.
Technip Energies removed from the Buy list primarily on valuation after strong share-price performance, though still seen as well positioned in LNG.
Field trip takeaways cite strong High NA momentum, a deep moat, installed base upgrades, and Match Act concerns as overdone.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees LNG FID capacity up 23% to about 280 mtpa across 2025-30 and prefers GTT.

earnings_insights: NKT Q3: operating EBITDA 4% below consensus, with weaker than expected Transmission and Distribution top line. Guidance maintained, with year-end expected at the high end of the range, about EUR 430m versus consensus EUR 424m.

Halma 1H: organic growth +12.3% reported versus consensus +11.5%, about a 5% beat. Safety outperformed, E&A including photonics missed. Photonics grew +30% in 1H and is guided to about +30% for the full year, which GS calls light as expectations have been falling.
